main_text.p: que cum trina dimensione gravitatem quantamcunque habere, ac leve esse corpus respectu gravioris, majorini-su ad gravitatis centrum vergentis, sicque corpus levius e sua sede depel-lentis, quod adeò cogatur rectâ lineâ sursum à centro eniti ad circumferen-tiam, cùm nulla ratio detur, cur po-tius divergat ad latus unum quàm al-terum: at corpora æque gravia nec in-vicem depellere, nec ab invicem de-pelli; sed corpus quodcunque, in cor-pore alio æque gravi, quantumvis li-quido positum, (v. g. aquam, aut aliud corpus quodcunque, eandem cum aqua, gravitatem obtinens, hoc est, sub æquali mole æquale pondus habens, in aqua,) non gravitare nec levitare; hoc est,nec deorsum nec sursum move-ri, sed datum quemcunque locum ser-vare. Sed quid hæc similitudo gravitatem concercens, potest conferre, ad jun-gendam virtutem, quæ Pulveri sym-pathetico vel sanguini effuso inhesse crê-datur.

page.notes: The last line "T datur," is a catchword-like fragment at the foot right; it is printed as a line of text, transcribed as a foot line. Ligatures and long s rendered as plain s. Words "inhesse" and "crêdatur" are the printed hyphenated line ends "inéffe cré-" and "datur" and may be partly uncertain; the line-end hyphens were joined.
